question: Did gain calibration introduce the one fresh paraphrase-control flip, and is there a global gain interval that preserves both target calibration and selectivity?
status: Post-hoc boundary diagnostic only. Any numerically safe gain found here requires a later untouched-family confirmation before adoption.

predictions.pred_a_authority_population_finiteness_a: All bound results, capabilities, and builders match; all values are finite; exactly 41 model forwards execute.
predictions.pred_b_uncalibrated_gain_is_control_sele: Gain 1.0 has zero paraphrase-control flips under both cross-fits.
predictions.pred_c_control_flip_is_a_calibration_thr: At least one gain above 1.0 flips a control, while gains 0.75 and 1.0 do not.
predictions.pred_d_a_safe_calibrated_gain_exists: At gain 1.1 or 1.2, every task/cross-fit target projection is in [0.90,1.10], worst target residual is at most 0.15, and both cross-fits have zero control flips, margin RMS at most 0.10, and median KL at most 0.02.
predictions.pred_e_behavior_dose_is_monotone_and_cro: Every task/cross-fit behavior projection strictly increases with gain and the cross-fit difference is at most 0.10 at every task/gain.

decision: A-E passing diagnoses a calibration-induced threshold and identifies only a provisional safe interval. If B fails, the fresh control issue predates calibration. If D fails, retain the uncalibrated interface and close gain tuning. This run cannot prospectively release a selected gain.
